ui.setup.title: Game Setup
ui.setup.reveal_map_hint: The whole map is explored from the start.
ui.setup.no_fog_hint: You always see the whole map and every unit. Computer players are not affected.
ui.setup.sandbox_hint: Adds a sandbox panel to the game: control computer players and grant resources.
ui.setup.lock_teams_hint: Diplomatic stances cannot be changed during the game.
ui.setup.full_tech_tree_hint: Every civilization can research every technology and train every unit; civilization bonuses are removed.
ui.start.nomad.desc: Stone Age without a Town Center: you choose where to build it.
ui.start.post_iron.desc: Iron Age with every technology of your civilization already researched.
ui.setup.issue.single_team: All players are in the same team.
ui.setup.issue.invalid_seed: The seed must be a whole number from 0 to 4294967295.
ui.setup.issue.player_count: The number of players must be from 2 to 8.
ui.setup.issue.duplicate_color: Each player needs a different color.
ui.victory.standard.desc: Win by destroying all enemies, or by holding all ruins, all artifacts or a Wonder for 2000 years.

ui.action.build.name: Build
ui.action.build.desc: Open the list of buildings. Pick one and click the map to place it.
ui.action.repair.name: Repair
ui.action.repair.desc: Click a damaged building or ship to repair it.
ui.action.attack_move.name: Attack-move
ui.action.attack_move.desc: Move to a point, fighting enemies on the way.
ui.action.attack_ground.name: Attack ground
ui.action.attack_ground.desc: Click a point on the map to bombard it. The blast hurts every unit in it, your own included, and fells trees.
ui.action.stop.name: Stop
ui.action.stand_ground.name: Stand ground
ui.action.stand_ground.desc: Hold position: attack enemies in reach, but do not chase them. Press again to cancel.
ui.action.unload.name: Unload
ui.action.unload.desc: Click a shore to unload the cargo.
ui.action.rally.name: Rally point
ui.action.rally.desc: Click where new units should gather. A right click also sets it.
ui.action.delete.name: Delete
ui.action.delete.desc: Destroy the selected objects for good (Del). Only an unfinished building refunds its cost.
ui.action.back.name: Back
ui.action.next.name: More
ui.action.trade_food.name: Trade food
ui.action.trade_food.desc: Carry food to the docks of other players in exchange for gold.
ui.action.trade_wood.name: Trade wood
ui.action.trade_wood.desc: Carry wood to the docks of other players in exchange for gold.
ui.action.trade_stone.name: Trade stone
ui.action.trade_stone.desc: Carry stone to the docks of other players in exchange for gold.
ui.object.ruin.desc: Ancient ruins. Bring a unit close to capture them. In a standard game, holding all ruins for 2000 years brings victory.
ui.object.artifact.desc: An ancient artifact. Bring a unit close to capture it; enemies can take it away the same way. In a standard game, holding all artifacts for 2000 years brings victory.
ui.diplomacy.title: Diplomacy
ui.diplomacy.locked: Teams are locked: stances cannot be changed.
ui.sandbox.title: Sandbox
ui.sandbox.mode.passive.desc: Builds the economy and an army, defends the base, never attacks.
ui.sandbox.mode.off.desc: Gives no new orders; units finish what they were doing.
ui.sandbox.mode.frozen.desc: Stops every unit, cancels training and research, then gives no orders.

ui.civ.full_tech_tree: The full tech tree is on: in this game the restrictions and bonuses below do not apply.

resource.food.desc: Needed for villagers, most units, research and advancing ages. Comes from berries, hunting, fishing and farms.
resource.wood.desc: Needed for buildings, ships, archers and siege weapons. Chopped from trees.
resource.stone.desc: Needed for walls and towers. Mined from stone mines.
resource.gold.desc: Needed for advanced units and research. Mined from gold mines or earned by sea trade.
resource.berry_bush.desc: Source of food. Villagers gather berries and carry them to a Granary or the Town Center.
resource.tree.desc: Source of wood. Villagers chop it and carry the wood to a Storage Pit or the Town Center.
resource.gold_mine.desc: Source of gold. Villagers mine it and carry the gold to a Storage Pit or the Town Center.
resource.stone_mine.desc: Source of stone. Villagers mine it and carry the stone to a Storage Pit or the Town Center.
resource.shore_fish.desc: Source of food near the shore. Villagers fish here from land and carry the catch to a Storage Pit or the Town Center.
resource.deep_fish.desc: Source of food at sea. Only fishing vessels can reach it; they unload at a Dock.
resource.gazelle_carcass.desc: Meat left after a hunt. It rots over time, so gather it quickly. Villagers carry it to a Storage Pit or the Town Center.
resource.elephant_carcass.desc: Meat left after a hunt. It rots over time, so gather it quickly. Villagers carry it to a Storage Pit or the Town Center.
resource.lion_carcass.desc: Meat left after a hunt. It rots over time, so gather it quickly. Villagers carry it to a Storage Pit or the Town Center.
resource.alligator_carcass.desc: Meat left after a hunt. It rots over time, so gather it quickly. Villagers carry it to a Storage Pit or the Town Center.
map.small_islands.desc: Every player starts on a small island. Land is scarce: ships and transports are essential.
map.large_islands.desc: Large islands separated by sea. There is room to build, but enemies are reached by ship.
map.coastal.desc: One landmass with the sea along its edges: both land armies and fleets matter.
map.inland.desc: Almost all land and hardly any water. Land armies decide everything.
map.highland.desc: All land with tall hills. Attacks from high ground deal more damage.
map.sandbox.desc: Flat land without water or cliffs. Plenty of wood, gold, stone and food right next to every start.
unit.villager.name: Villager
unit.villager.desc: Gathers food, wood, stone and gold, constructs and repairs buildings. The base of your economy: the more villagers work, the faster you grow.
unit.clubman.name: Clubman
unit.clubman.desc: The cheapest infantry, available from the start. Weak, but useful for early defense.
unit.axeman.name: Axeman
unit.axeman.desc: Infantry with more hit points and attack than the Clubman.
unit.short_swordsman.name: Short Swordsman
unit.short_swordsman.desc: Armored sword infantry of the Bronze Age. Costs food and gold.
unit.broad_swordsman.name: Broad Swordsman
unit.broad_swordsman.desc: Sword infantry with more hit points and attack.
unit.long_swordsman.name: Long Swordsman
unit.long_swordsman.desc: Heavy sword infantry with better armor.
unit.legion.name: Legion
unit.legion.desc: Elite sword infantry with twice the hit points of a Long Swordsman.
unit.hoplite.name: Hoplite
unit.hoplite.desc: Slow infantry with a very strong attack and heavy armor. Has no protection from arrows.
unit.phalanx.name: Phalanx
unit.phalanx.desc: Hoplite with more attack and armor.
unit.centurion.name: Centurion
unit.centurion.desc: Elite heavy infantry, the strongest foot soldier.
unit.scout.name: Scout
unit.scout.desc: Fast rider with a long line of sight. Weak in combat: use it to explore the map.
unit.cavalry.name: Cavalry
unit.cavalry.desc: Fast, durable rider. Deals bonus damage to Barracks infantry.
unit.heavy_cavalry.name: Heavy Cavalry
unit.heavy_cavalry.desc: Armored cavalry with more attack. Deals bonus damage to Barracks infantry.
unit.cataphract.name: Cataphract
unit.cataphract.desc: Elite cavalry in heavy armor. Deals bonus damage to Barracks infantry.
unit.chariot.name: Chariot
unit.chariot.desc: Fast unit that costs no gold. Resists conversion and deals double damage to priests. Requires the Wheel.
unit.war_elephant.name: War Elephant
unit.war_elephant.desc: Slow and expensive, but extremely durable. Damages all adjacent enemy units at once.
unit.bowman.name: Bowman
unit.bowman.desc: Basic archer: attacks from a distance, but falls quickly in close combat.
unit.improved_bowman.name: Improved Bowman
unit.improved_bowman.desc: Archer with more range and attack.
unit.composite_bowman.name: Composite Bowman
unit.composite_bowman.desc: The best foot archer, with the longest range.
unit.chariot_archer.name: Chariot Archer
unit.chariot_archer.desc: Fast archer that costs no gold. Resists conversion and deals triple damage to priests. Requires the Wheel.
unit.elephant_archer.name: Elephant Archer
unit.horse_archer.name: Horse Archer
unit.horse_archer.desc: Very fast mounted archer with armor against arrows. Good at striking and retreating.
unit.heavy_horse_archer.name: Heavy Horse Archer
unit.heavy_horse_archer.desc: Elite mounted archer: faster and more durable.
unit.stone_thrower.name: Stone Thrower
unit.stone_thrower.desc: Siege weapon with huge area damage, excellent against buildings and groups. Cannot hit targets right next to it; slow and fragile, so keep it guarded.
unit.catapult.name: Catapult
unit.catapult.desc: Siege weapon with a longer range and a wider blast. Cannot hit targets right next to it.
unit.heavy_catapult.name: Heavy Catapult
unit.heavy_catapult.desc: The strongest siege weapon: more hit points, range and the widest blast. Cannot hit targets right next to it.
unit.ballista.name: Ballista
unit.ballista.desc: Fires heavy bolts at a single target from a long range. Cannot hit targets right next to it.
unit.helepolis.name: Helepolis
unit.helepolis.desc: Rapid-fire ballista with a longer range. Cannot hit targets right next to it.
unit.priest.name: Priest
unit.priest.desc: Heals friendly units and converts enemy units to your side. Conversion takes time and spends faith, which then recharges. Unarmed and fragile.
unit.fishing_boat.name: Fishing Boat
unit.fishing_boat.desc: Catches fish at sea and carries it to the Dock.
unit.fishing_ship.name: Fishing Ship
unit.trade_boat.name: Trade Boat
unit.trade_boat.desc: Carries food, wood or stone from your Dock to the Dock of another player and brings back gold. Choose the goods on its panel.
unit.merchant_ship.name: Merchant Ship
unit.merchant_ship.desc: Faster and sturdier trade vessel. Carries goods to the Dock of another player and brings back gold.
unit.light_transport.name: Light Transport
unit.light_transport.desc: Carries up to 5 land units across water. Use Unload and click a shore to land them.
unit.heavy_transport.name: Heavy Transport
unit.heavy_transport.desc: Faster transport that carries up to 10 land units.
unit.scout_ship.name: Scout Ship
unit.scout_ship.desc: Light war ship. Attacks ships and targets near the shore.
unit.war_galley.name: War Galley
unit.war_galley.desc: War ship with more hit points, attack and range.
unit.trireme.name: Trireme
unit.trireme.desc: Heavy war ship of the Iron Age.
unit.catapult_trireme.name: Catapult Trireme
unit.catapult_trireme.desc: Ship with a catapult: area damage, excellent against buildings on the shore. Cannot hit targets right next to it.
unit.juggernaut.name: Juggernaut
unit.juggernaut.desc: Heavy catapult ship with more hit points, range and a wider blast.
unit.gazelle.name: Gazelle
unit.gazelle.desc: Prey: runs away from hunters. Send villagers to hunt it for meat.
unit.elephant.name: Elephant
unit.elephant.desc: Large prey with a lot of meat. Fights back, so hunt it with several villagers.
unit.lion.name: Lion
unit.lion.desc: Predator: attacks units that come close. Leaves a little meat when killed.
unit.alligator.name: Alligator
unit.alligator.desc: Predator: attacks units that come close. Leaves a little meat when killed.
building.town_center.name: Town Center
building.town_center.desc: The heart of your settlement: trains villagers, advances to the next age and accepts every resource. Gives housing for 4. Additional Town Centers need a Government Center.
building.house.name: House
building.house.desc: Adds housing for 4 units. Units cannot be trained without free housing, so build houses ahead of time.
building.barracks.name: Barracks
building.barracks.desc: Trains infantry: clubmen, later axemen and swordsmen. Required for the Archery Range and the Stable. Counts toward the Tool Age.
building.granary.name: Granary
building.granary.desc: Villagers bring berries and farm food here, so build it next to berry bushes and farms. Researches walls and towers. Required for the Market. Counts toward the Tool Age.
building.storage_pit.name: Storage Pit
building.storage_pit.desc: Villagers bring wood, stone, gold, meat and shore fish here, so build it next to forests, mines and hunting grounds. Researches weapons, armor and shields. Counts toward the Tool Age.
building.dock.name: Dock
building.dock.desc: Built on the shore. Builds fishing, trade, transport and war ships. Fishing vessels unload their catch here and trade vessels bring their gold. Counts toward the Tool Age.
building.farm.name: Farm
building.farm.desc: A steady source of food worked by one villager. Its supply is finite: when it runs out, the farm disappears and a new one has to be built. Place it next to a Granary or the Town Center. Requires a Market.
building.archery_range.name: Archery Range
building.archery_range.desc: Trains archers: bowmen, later chariot, horse and elephant archers. Required for the Siege Workshop. Counts toward the Bronze Age.
building.stable.name: Stable
building.stable.desc: Trains mounted units: scouts, later cavalry, chariots and war elephants. Required for the Academy. Counts toward the Bronze Age.
building.market.name: Market
building.market.desc: Researches upgrades for woodcutting, mining and farms, and the Wheel. Allows building farms. Required for the Government Center and the Temple. Counts toward the Bronze Age.
building.academy.name: Academy
building.academy.desc: Trains hoplites: slow but very strong heavy infantry. Counts toward the Iron Age.
building.government_center.name: Government Center
building.government_center.desc: Researches advanced technologies: Architecture, Nobility, Writing, Ballistics and others. Allows building additional Town Centers. Counts toward the Iron Age.
building.siege_workshop.name: Siege Workshop
building.siege_workshop.desc: Builds siege weapons, stone throwers and ballistas, which destroy buildings and walls from afar. Counts toward the Iron Age.
building.temple.name: Temple
building.temple.desc: Trains priests, who heal your units and convert enemy ones, and researches upgrades for them. Counts toward the Iron Age.
building.wonder.name: Wonder
building.wonder.desc: A monument of the Iron Age. In a standard game its owner wins if it stands for 2000 years. Every player is told about it, so be ready to defend it.
building.small_wall.name: Small Wall
building.small_wall.desc: Blocks the way for land units. Drag to build a line. Unlocked by the Small Wall research at the Granary.
building.medium_wall.name: Medium Wall
building.medium_wall.desc: A stronger wall that blocks the way for land units. Drag to build a line.
building.fortification.name: Fortification
building.fortification.desc: The strongest wall that blocks the way for land units. Drag to build a line.
building.watch_tower.name: Watch Tower
building.watch_tower.desc: Shoots at enemies in range on its own. Unlocked by the Watch Tower research at the Granary.
building.sentry_tower.name: Sentry Tower
building.sentry_tower.desc: A sturdier tower with more attack and range. Shoots at enemies in range on its own.
building.guard_tower.name: Guard Tower
building.guard_tower.desc: A heavy tower with a long range. Shoots at enemies in range on its own.
building.ballista_tower.name: Ballista Tower
building.ballista_tower.desc: A tower that fires heavy ballista bolts: far more damage per shot, but a slower rate of fire.
tech.tool_age.name: Tool Age
tech.tool_age.desc: Advance to the Tool Age: new buildings, units and research. Needs two different buildings out of Barracks, Granary, Storage Pit and Dock.
tech.bronze_age.name: Bronze Age
tech.bronze_age.desc: Advance to the Bronze Age: new buildings, units and research. Needs two different buildings out of Archery Range, Stable and Market.
tech.iron_age.name: Iron Age
tech.iron_age.desc: Advance to the Iron Age: the strongest units and research. Needs two different buildings out of Academy, Government Center, Siege Workshop and Temple.

tech.metalworking.name: Metalworking

tech.iron_shield.name: Iron Shield

tech.small_wall.name: Small Wall
tech.small_wall.desc: Allows villagers to build small walls.
tech.medium_wall.name: Medium Wall
tech.fortification.name: Fortification
tech.watch_tower.name: Watch Tower
tech.watch_tower.desc: Allows villagers to build watch towers.
tech.sentry_tower.name: Sentry Tower
tech.guard_tower.name: Guard Tower
tech.ballista_tower.name: Ballista Tower
tech.ballista_tower.desc: Upgrades towers to ballista towers. Requires Ballistics.
tech.battle_axe.name: Battle Axe
tech.short_sword.name: Short Sword
tech.broad_sword.name: Broad Sword
tech.broad_sword.desc: Upgrades Short Swordsmen to Broad Swordsmen.
tech.long_sword.name: Long Sword
tech.long_sword.desc: Upgrades Broad Swordsmen to Long Swordsmen.
tech.legion.name: Legion
tech.legion.desc: Upgrades Long Swordsmen to Legions. Requires Fanaticism.
tech.war_galley.name: War Galley
tech.war_galley.desc: Upgrades Scout Ships to War Galleys.
tech.trireme.name: Trireme
tech.catapult_trireme.name: Catapult Trireme
tech.catapult_trireme.desc: Allows building Catapult Triremes. Requires Trireme.
tech.juggernaut.name: Juggernaut
tech.juggernaut.desc: Upgrades Catapult Triremes to Juggernauts. Requires Engineering.
tech.fishing_ship.name: Fishing Ship
tech.fishing_ship.desc: Upgrades Fishing Boats to Fishing Ships.
tech.merchant_ship.name: Merchant Ship
tech.merchant_ship.desc: Upgrades Trade Boats to Merchant Ships.
tech.heavy_transport.name: Heavy Transport
tech.heavy_transport.desc: Upgrades Light Transports to Heavy Transports.
tech.improved_bow.name: Improved Bow
tech.composite_bow.name: Composite Bow
tech.composite_bow.desc: Upgrades Improved Bowmen to Composite Bowmen.
tech.heavy_horse_archer.name: Heavy Horse Archer
tech.heavy_horse_archer.desc: Upgrades Horse Archers to Heavy Horse Archers. Requires Chain Mail (Archers).
tech.heavy_cavalry.name: Heavy Cavalry
tech.cataphract.name: Cataphract
tech.cataphract.desc: Upgrades Heavy Cavalry to Cataphracts. Requires Metallurgy.
tech.woodworking.name: Woodworking
tech.woodworking.desc: Villagers carry +2 wood per trip; +1 range for ranged units and towers.
tech.artisanship.name: Artisanship
tech.artisanship.desc: Villagers carry +2 wood per trip; +1 range for ranged units and towers.
tech.craftsmanship.name: Craftsmanship
tech.craftsmanship.desc: Villagers carry +2 wood per trip; +1 range for ranged units and towers.
tech.stone_mining.name: Stone Mining
tech.siegecraft.name: Siegecraft
tech.siegecraft.desc: Villagers carry +3 stone per trip and can destroy walls and towers.
tech.gold_mining.name: Gold Mining
tech.coinage.name: Coinage
tech.coinage.desc: +25% gold mining speed; tribute is sent without tax.
tech.domestication.name: Domestication
tech.plow.name: Plow
tech.irrigation.name: Irrigation
tech.wheel.name: Wheel
tech.wheel.desc: Villagers move much faster; allows Chariots and Chariot Archers.
tech.architecture.name: Architecture
tech.architecture.desc: Buildings are built 33% faster and have +20% hit points.
tech.nobility.name: Nobility
tech.nobility.desc: +15% hit points for chariots, cavalry and horse archers.
tech.writing.name: Writing
tech.writing.desc: Allies share the areas they have explored.
tech.aristocracy.name: Aristocracy
tech.alchemy.name: Alchemy
tech.alchemy.desc: +1 attack for ranged units and towers.
tech.ballistics.name: Ballistics
tech.ballistics.desc: Ranged and siege units hit moving targets.
tech.engineering.name: Engineering
tech.engineering.desc: +2 range for siege weapons and catapult ships.
tech.astrology.name: Astrology
tech.mysticism.name: Mysticism
tech.mysticism.desc: Doubles the hit points of priests.
tech.polytheism.name: Polytheism
tech.fanaticism.name: Fanaticism
tech.monotheism.name: Monotheism
tech.monotheism.desc: Priests convert buildings and enemy priests.
tech.afterlife.name: Afterlife
tech.jihad.name: Jihad
tech.jihad.desc: Villagers: 65 hit points, 10 attack, faster; carry capacity −8.
tech.phalanx.name: Phalanx
tech.centurion.name: Centurion
tech.centurion.desc: Upgrades Phalanxes to Centurions. Requires Aristocracy.
tech.catapult.name: Catapult
tech.heavy_catapult.name: Heavy Catapult
tech.heavy_catapult.desc: Upgrades Catapults to Heavy Catapults. Requires Siegecraft.
tech.helepolis.name: Helepolis
tech.helepolis.desc: Upgrades Ballistas to Helepolises. Requires Craftsmanship.
civ.assyrian.name: Assyrian
civ.assyrian.desc: Raiders with a fast start: villagers move quicker, and Bowmen, Chariot Archers and Horse Archers shoot faster than anyone else. A full Siege Workshop, Legions and Cataphracts carry the late game, but armor upgrades stop early and there are no elephants, no Phalanx and no improved bows.
civ.assyrian.bonuses: Bowman line, Chariot Archers and horse archers fire 1/3 faster; villagers move 1/3 faster.
civ.babylonian.name: Babylonian
civ.babylonian.desc: A defensive civilization: walls and towers are twice as tough, stone is mined faster and priests recover their faith sooner. A full Temple, Legions and Heavy Catapults are available. The navy stops at the War Galley, and there is no heavy cavalry, no elephants and no Ballista.
civ.babylonian.bonuses: Walls and towers have double hit points; priest faith recharges 12 s faster; stone mining +30%.
civ.choson.name: Choson
civ.choson.desc: Built around the toughest swordsmen in the game: Long Swordsmen and Legions get +80 hit points. Longer-range towers and cheap priests back them up; Cataphracts, Triremes and Helepolis are available. No chariots, no elephants, no late Academy infantry, and siege throwers stop at the Stone Thrower.
civ.choson.bonuses: Long Swordsman and Legion +80 hit points; tower range +2; priests cost 1/3 less.
civ.egyptian.name: Egyptian
civ.egyptian.desc: A civilization of chariots and priests: Chariots and Chariot Archers are tougher, priests convert from further away and gold is mined faster. War Elephants, Elephant Archers and a full navy are available. No Cavalry, no Horse Archers, swordsmen stop at the Short Swordsman and siege at the Stone Thrower.
civ.egyptian.bonuses: Priest range +3; gold mining +20%; Chariot and Chariot Archer hit points +1/3.
civ.greek.name: Greek
civ.greek.desc: Masters of the Academy and the sea: Hoplites, Phalanxes, Centurions and war ships move 30% faster. A full Siege Workshop, a full navy and Heavy Cavalry are available. Archery is limited to the plain Bowman, swordsmen stop at the Short Swordsman, and there are no chariots, no Horse Archers and no elephants.
civ.greek.bonuses: Hoplite, Phalanx, Centurion and war ships move 30% faster.
civ.hittite.name: Hittite
civ.hittite.desc: Siege and archery: Stone Throwers and Catapults have double hit points, every archer hits harder and war ships out-range the enemy. Elephants, chariots, Heavy Horse Archers and Centurions are available. The Temple is almost bare, the navy stops at the War Galley, and there is no Ballista, no heavy cavalry and no Legion.
civ.hittite.bonuses: Stone Thrower, Catapult and Heavy Catapult have double hit points; archer attack +1; war ship range +4.
civ.minoan.name: Minoan
civ.minoan.desc: A sea power: ships cost a third less, farms hold more food and Composite Bowmen out-range other archers. A full navy, a full Siege Workshop and Centurions are available. Defenses stop at the Sentry Tower and the Medium Wall, the Temple is weak, and there are no chariots, no elephants, no Horse Archers and no heavy cavalry.
civ.minoan.bonuses: Ships cost 1/3 less; Composite Bowman range +2; farm food +25%.
civ.persian.name: Persian
civ.persian.desc: Hunters and elephant riders: hunting is 30% faster, elephants move 50% faster and Triremes fire faster. Full cavalry up to the Cataphract, Heavy Horse Archers and Legions are available. The economy pays for it: farms hold 30% less food, most Market upgrades and the Wheel are missing, and so are chariots, the Ballista and late Academy infantry.
civ.persian.bonuses: Hunting +30%; farm food −30%; elephants move 50% faster; Triremes fire 50% faster.
civ.phoenician.name: Phoenician
civ.phoenician.desc: Woodcutters and sailors: villagers carry more wood, Catapult Triremes and Juggernauts fire much faster and elephants cost 25% less. A full navy, Legions, Centurions and chariots are available. Siege stops at the Stone Thrower, and there are no Horse Archers and no heavy cavalry.
civ.phoenician.bonuses: Elephants cost 25% less; Catapult Triremes and Juggernauts fire 2/3 faster; woodcutting +2.
civ.shang.name: Shang
civ.shang.desc: The fastest economic start: villagers cost 30% less, and walls are twice as tough. Full cavalry up to the Cataphract, Heavy Horse Archers, chariots and the Helepolis are available. The navy stops at the War Galley, and there are no elephants, no Long Swordsmen or Legions and no late Academy infantry.
civ.shang.bonuses: Villagers cost 30% less; walls have double hit points.
civ.sumerian.name: Sumerian
civ.sumerian.desc: Farmers and siege engineers: farms hold twice the food, villagers are tougher, and Stone Throwers and Catapults fire 50% faster. War Elephants, chariots, Heavy Horse Archers and Centurions are available. No Cavalry, no Ballista, no improved bows, and the Temple is weak.
civ.sumerian.bonuses: Villagers +15 hit points; Stone Thrower line fires 50% faster; farm food doubled.
civ.yamato.name: Yamato
civ.yamato.desc: Cavalry and navy: Scouts, the Cavalry line and Horse Archers cost 25% less, ships are a third tougher and villagers move faster. A full navy, Cataphracts, Heavy Horse Archers and Centurions are available. Defenses and the Temple are weak, swordsmen stop at the Short Swordsman, siege at the Stone Thrower, and there are no chariots and no elephants.
civ.yamato.bonuses: Horse Archers, Scouts and the Cavalry line cost 25% less; villagers move 1/3 faster; ships +1/3 hit points.
